content.question_text: What are abstract methods in Java?

core_requirements: Methods that do not need an implementation (no body).
acceptable_variations: Methods that are only declared, not implemented.

content.question_text: What happens to a class if one of its methods is declared as abstract?

core_requirements: The class itself must be declared as abstract.

content.question_text: What is the purpose of abstract methods?

core_requirements: They act as placeholders for methods that are implemented in subclasses.
acceptable_variations: To force subclasses to provide their own implementation.
They define a contract for subclasses.

content.question_text: Can an abstract class have fields?
Can an abstract class have concrete methods?

core_requirements: Methods that are not declared as abstract.
They have a full implementation (method body).

content.question_text: What are the two choices when a subclass extends an abstract class?

core_requirements: It can leave some or all abstract methods undefined — then the subclass must be declared abstract as well.
Or it can define all abstract methods — then the subclass is no longer abstract.
acceptable_variations: Implement all abstract methods or become abstract itself.

content.question_text: Can you declare an abstract class that does not contain any abstract methods?
What happens to a class when it is declared as abstract?

core_requirements: It cannot be instantiated (no objects of that class can be created).
acceptable_variations: You cannot create objects of that class.

content.question_text: Can you create an object variable of an abstract class? What type of object does it need to refer to?

core_requirements: Yes, you can create object variables of an abstract class.
Such a variable must refer to an object of a nonabstract (concrete) subclass.
acceptable_variations: Variable can be declared, but it must point to a concrete subclass instance.

content.question_text: How can an abstract class variable call an abstract method when it refers to a concrete subclass?

core_requirements: The variable never refers to an object of the abstract class (it's impossible to construct one).
The variable always refers to an object of a concrete subclass where the method is defined.
The compiler allows the call because the abstract method is declared in the abstract class.
acceptable_variations: The variable points to a concrete subclass where the method is implemented.
Since the abstract method is declared in the superclass, the compiler accepts it.
